The notes also confirm that sampling occurs at voxel centers (implied by the grid sampling of the volume tensor) and that the method is adapted for volume-supervised training.

Unlike the original 3DGS which uses calibrated multi-view RGB images for novel-view synthesis, AVIS uses a 3D volume plus aligned ROI mask as input, samples Gaussian initialization from voxels inside the mask (rather than sparse SfM points), and optimizes toward mask density or CT intensity via losses on rasterized voxel grids [S1, unofficial].

The claim accurately reflects the information provided in Source [S1]. The source explicitly states that AVIS uses a 3D volume plus aligned ROI mask as input (unlike original 3DGS which uses calibrated multi-view RGB images), samples Gaussian initialization from voxels inside the mask (rather than sparse SfM points), and optimizes toward mask density or CT intensity via losses on rasterized voxel grids.
